rules: 1. Name starts with an environment prefix -> environment
2. Name starts with a presentation prefix -> presentation
3. Body prefix AND (hidden in viewport or render OR name contains a backup marker) -> excluded_backup
4. Body prefix AND an enabled Armature modifier targeting armature_object -> body
5. Anything else -> unresolved (reported, never silently included)
classification.basis: Prefixes observed in the source and in docs/env_warehouse_phase1.md / cinematic_pass_v1.py; skin binding per scripts/rig/skin_rigid_v01.py. Not an approved project rule.

float_compare.basis: Blender stores vertex coordinates as float32; the unit-in-last-place at |x|~2.5 m is ~2.4e-7 m, so 1e-6 m is ~4 ulp of margin.

coincident_vertex.basis: Same float32 argument: points closer than this are numerically the same location.

near_duplicate_vertex.basis: Blender's Merge by Distance default (0.0001 m). A tool default, not a project requirement.

degenerate_face_area.basis: (coincident_vertex)^2: a face below this area cannot be distinguished from a line/point at float32 precision.

midline_band.basis: Half-width of the band around the mirror plane treated as 'midline' when classifying physical side. No spec value exists.

symmetry_match.basis: 1 mm, chosen as a diagnostic threshold only. No specification sets a symmetry tolerance; findings using it stay provisional.

bone_pair_position.basis: 1 mm. phase_mirror.md requires mirrored bones but states no tolerance.

grid_cell.basis: Not used for nearest-neighbour (exact k-d tree, U-GEOM-04). Retained only as documentation; coincident-pair search uses a grid whose cell equals the pair tolerance.

bone_min_length_for_direction.basis: float32 endpoints at ~1 m carry ~1.2e-7 m error; on a 1e-4 m bone that is <=0.14 deg of direction error, well under the 1 deg pair tolerance. Shorter bones get no direction value and are reported as near-zero-length.

tri_plane_coplanar.basis: float32 world coordinates at ~1 m carry ~1e-7 m error; two triangles within 1e-6 m of each other's plane are treated as coplanar.

tri_contact.basis: Equal to coincident_vertex: triangles closer than this without a proper crossing are 'contact' (touching), not separated.

max_candidate_pairs.basis: Memory/time guard for BVH candidate pairs per mesh or mesh pair; exceeding it yields UNABLE_TO_DETERMINE, never a clean result.

proximity_search_radius.basis: Reporting scope only: mesh pairs farther apart than this are not measured. No project document defines a proximity requirement; this is not a defect threshold.

penetration_null_volume.basis: Overlap volumes at or below this are reported as zero overlap. 1e-12 m^3 is a 1 um slab over 1 mm^2, the tri_contact scale over a face of that size. No specification sets a volume threshold. Checked against zero-overlap fixtures (U-SOL-02, B-VOL-03) and Boolean residuals.

penetration_bisection_iterations.basis: Bisection bracket T <= ~0.6 m for body pairs; after 18 halvings the bracket is <= 2.3 um, the resolution of the axial separation bound.

volume_solver_agreement_rel.basis: Two independent Boolean kernels (EXACT, MANIFOLD) and both operand orders must agree on the intersection volume to 0.01%. A larger spread leaves the volume unvalidated (SOLVER_DISAGREEMENT).

volume_identity_rel.basis: V(A n B) + V(A minus B) must equal V(A) to 0.01%, computed with an independent DIFFERENCE operation. Failure leaves the volume unvalidated (IDENTITY_FAILED).

penetration_axial_scan_samples.basis: Uniform samples of the overlap volume along each axial translation ray (spacing T/32, T <= ~0.6 m for body pairs => <= 1.9 cm). The scan only DETECTS non-monotone overlap wider than the spacing and selects the first null sample before bisecting; it cannot prove that no narrower gap exists, so it never upgrades a result to an exact minimum (U-SOL-11, U-SOL-12).

coordinate_convention.world_frame: Blender world, right-handed, metres (scene METRIC, scale_length 1.0 verified per run)

label_interpretations.V_viewer_relative: Unsided bones and *_R meshes (+X) are 'right' as seen from the front camera at -Y. This is how phase_mirror.md, anim_hello.md and the manifest use 'right'.
label_interpretations.A_anatomical: Labels name the robot's own sides. Then +X is the robot's LEFT and every current side label is inverted.

coordinate_convention.note: Pair-wise mirror measurements are label-independent and may run; deciding which side is correct, renaming, and anatomical deformation tests may not.

severity_definitions.BLOCKER: Prevents a correct export/runtime result or invalidates downstream analysis until resolved.
severity_definitions.HIGH: Likely to produce visibly wrong behaviour or wrong engineering decisions if left; resolve before structural work.
severity_definitions.MEDIUM: Contradicts a written project convention or spec, or weakens maintainability, without a demonstrated runtime failure.
severity_definitions.LOW: Diagnostic deviation with plausible design intent; review when convenient.
severity_definitions.INFO: Recorded fact for context; no action implied.

M-CLASSIFY.property: Object class: body / environment / presentation / excluded_backup / unresolved
M-CLASSIFY.includes: all scene objects of type MESH
M-CLASSIFY.failure_modes: a new naming pattern falls to 'unresolved'

M-BBOX-WORLD.definition: min/max over matrix_world @ vertex.co (base mesh data)
M-BBOX-WORLD.failure_modes: wrong inclusion set; modifiers that add geometry are ignored
M-BBOX-WORLD.cannot_prove: presentation silhouette after modifiers or pose

M-BBOX-EVAL.definition: min/max over evaluated mesh vertices x matrix_world
M-BBOX-EVAL.geometry: evaluated at the file's current frame
M-BBOX-EVAL.failure_modes: depends on current frame / active action pose
M-BBOX-EVAL.proves: what the depsgraph produces at that frame

M-TOPO.property: Boundary, non-manifold, wire edges; loose vertices; connected components
M-TOPO.definition: edge face-incidence from polygons (1 = boundary, >2 = non-manifold, 0 = wire); union-find over edges
M-TOPO.failure_modes: none known for the counted properties
M-TOPO.cannot_prove: that an open boundary is unintended

M-DEGEN.definition: Newell polygon area <= degenerate_face_area; edge length <= zero_length_edge
M-DEGEN.failure_modes: non-planar n-gons use Newell projected area

M-DUP.definition: unordered pairs within tolerance, exact grid search
M-DUP.cannot_prove: that they are unintended (seams, split normals)

M-SYM-MESH.definition: nearest-neighbour distance from mirrored points to the comparison set, both directions
M-SYM-MESH.includes: body objects / named L-R mesh pairs
M-SYM-MESH.failure_modes: unequal vertex density inflates distances; NN can match the wrong surface
M-SYM-MESH.proves: upper bound on surface mismatch at sampled vertices

M-BONE-WORLD.property: Bone head/tail world positions and lengths

M-GRAPH.property: Roots, components, cycles, depth, leaves, missing parents

M-SIDE-PARSE.definition: suffix (_L/_R/.L/.R) then infix (_L_/_R_) parsing; pair by base name
M-SIDE-PARSE.failure_modes: a name containing a lone 'L'/'R' token that is not a side marker

M-FACING.property: Forward axis and anatomical right axis
M-FACING.definition: sign of independent front/back cue offsets along Y; right = forward x up
M-FACING.cannot_prove: which labelling convention the owner intends

M-SYM-BONE.definition: |mirror(head_a) - head_b|, same for tail, |len_a - len_b|, angle(mirror(dir_a), dir_b)
M-SYM-BONE.failure_modes: roll is not compared (reflection flips handedness)

M-COLOC.property: Distance from a MECH/CTRL bone head to the nearest DEF bone head
M-COLOC.definition: min over DEF bones of |head - def_head|
M-COLOC.failure_modes: nearest DEF may not be the logically driven one
M-COLOC.proves: where mechanism bones sit relative to the deform skeleton

M-SKIN.property: Skinning conditions 1-4 (deform flag, group exists, non-zero weights, bound via Armature modifier)
M-SKIN.definition: set logic over bones, vertex groups, weights and modifiers

M-CONSTRAINT-REF.definition: lookup against scene objects and armature bones
M-CONSTRAINT-REF.failure_modes: constraint types with unusual target fields
M-CONSTRAINT-REF.cannot_prove: mathematical correctness of a valid constraint

M-CONSTRAINT-PAIR.property: Constraint stack equality across mirror pairs
M-CONSTRAINT-PAIR.definition: compare (type, side-stripped subtarget, influence, spaces, mute) stacks

M-SPEC-COMPARE.includes: keys with an agreed landmark definition
M-SPEC-COMPARE.failure_modes: landmark definitions for most SPEC_JSON keys are not documented

M-NORMALS.definition: edges shared by exactly two faces must be traversed in opposite directions; signed volume (divergence theorem) is positive for outward-wound closed shells
M-NORMALS.frame: object local (sign interpreted with the object matrix determinant)
M-NORMALS.transforms: local coordinates; negative-determinant objects flip the world-space meaning
M-NORMALS.failure_modes: open or non-manifold meshes get no volume; self-intersecting shells give misleading volume
M-NORMALS.proves: inconsistent neighbour winding exists; closed shell is inside-out
M-NORMALS.cannot_prove: that custom split normals or shading are correct

M-SELFINT.geometry: base (unmodified) mesh data, Blender loop-triangle tessellation
M-SELFINT.property: Triangles of one mesh that cross, overlap coplanarly or fold over (non-adjacent or adjacent)
M-SELFINT.definition: TriBVH box candidates -> welded-vertex adjacency filter (edge-sharing: fold-over only; vertex-sharing: opposite-edge crossing or coplanar overlap) -> exact classifier
M-SELFINT.includes: body meshes; degenerate triangles are excluded and listed
M-SELFINT.failure_modes: adjacency uses welded positions (weld = coincident_vertex), so genuinely separate surfaces welded by coincidence are not reported; budget exceeded -> UNABLE_TO_DETERMINE
M-SELFINT.proves: listed triangle pairs intersect by the stated definitions
M-SELFINT.cannot_prove: absence of self-intersection (no result is a clean bill of health); intent; behaviour of evaluated (modifier) geometry

M-DEFORM-TEST.property: Evaluated mesh displacement when a control bone is posed (isolated copy)
M-DEFORM-TEST.definition: rest snapshot vs posed snapshot of depsgraph-evaluated vertices; pose restored and verified
M-DEFORM-TEST.includes: body meshes; CTRL flex-type bones, one axis, fixed angle
M-DEFORM-TEST.failure_modes: constraint limits clamp the response; animation must be detached (copy only)
M-DEFORM-TEST.proves: which meshes follow a control bone and by how much at that pose
M-DEFORM-TEST.cannot_prove: motion quality, ranges of motion, or any anatomical claim

M-THUMB-ADJ.property: Which finger base each thumb sits beside
M-THUMB-ADJ.definition: compare |thumb CMC head - Index MCP head| with |... - Little MCP head|
M-THUMB-ADJ.includes: DEF thumb/finger bones of each hand
M-THUMB-ADJ.cannot_prove: which hand the owner treats as correct

M-SHORT-BONE.proves: the bone has no numerically meaningful direction/roll

M-EXPORT-PROBE.property: Skin joint set of an exported GLB (all bones vs deform-only)
M-EXPORT-PROBE.definition: export a selected body+armature from an isolated copy, read nodes/skins from the GLB JSON chunk
M-EXPORT-PROBE.failure_modes: exporter option semantics can change between Blender versions
M-EXPORT-PROBE.proves: which bones the exporter writes as joints with the given options

M-GATE.property: Side-dependent operations refuse to decide while the convention is unresolved
M-GATE.definition: core/gate.py reads coordinate_convention.status and the allow flag

M-REGRESS.definition: compare source hash, metrics, method statuses, tests and findings of two QA runs
M-REGRESS.failure_modes: findings are keyed by title, so a retitled finding appears as removed+added
M-REGRESS.proves: differences between runs; nondeterminism when the source hash is identical

M-NORMALS-BLENDER.property: Faces Blender's recalc_face_normals would flip (independent orientation algorithm)
M-NORMALS-BLENDER.definition: bmesh copy, normal_update, recalc_face_normals, count faces whose normal reversed
M-NORMALS-BLENDER.failure_modes: Blender's outside heuristic can misjudge complex shells
M-NORMALS-BLENDER.cannot_prove: that the current orientation is wrong by design

M-TRI-PAIR.geometry: base (unmodified) mesh data, Blender loop-triangle tessellation
M-TRI-PAIR.property: Triangle-pair relation: disjoint / contact / intersect (proper crossing) / coplanar_overlap / degenerate
M-TRI-PAIR.definition: degenerate if area<=degenerate_face_area or any edge<=tri_contact; coplanar = one triangle inside the other's tri_plane_coplanar slab -> clipped overlap area; else strict-interior edge crossing with depth > tri_contact = intersect (shallower = contact); else min distance vs tri_contact. Validated against a separating-axis oracle, an exact rational oracle and dense sampling.
M-TRI-PAIR.failure_modes: crossings exactly on a triangle boundary are classed 'contact' (touch), not 'intersect'; near-coplanar pairs depend on tri_plane_coplanar
M-TRI-PAIR.proves: the geometric relation of two triangles to numerical tolerance
M-TRI-PAIR.cannot_prove: that a relation is a design defect

M-INTERMESH.geometry: base (unmodified) mesh data, Blender loop-triangle tessellation
M-INTERMESH.property: Triangle intersections between two body meshes
M-INTERMESH.definition: TriBVH cross candidates -> exact classifier; pair status DEFINITE / POSSIBLE (contact only) / NONE_DETECTED / UNABLE_TO_DETERMINE
M-INTERMESH.failure_modes: volumetric penetration is only interpretable for closed manifold meshes (flagged per pair)
M-INTERMESH.proves: triangle-level intersections between the two meshes
M-INTERMESH.cannot_prove: whether overlap is intentional construction, or penetration depth

M-DISTANCE.geometry: base (unmodified) mesh data, Blender loop-triangle tessellation
M-DISTANCE.property: Exact minimum separation between two non-intersecting meshes, with the triangles and world points involved
M-DISTANCE.definition: branch-and-bound over TriBVH; triangle distance = min(vertex-face, edge-edge)
M-DISTANCE.failure_modes: pairs beyond the search radius are not measured; invalid for intersecting pairs (reported as intersecting)
M-DISTANCE.proves: the minimum distance to float precision
M-DISTANCE.cannot_prove: that a small distance is a defect

M-BVH.geometry: base (unmodified) mesh data, Blender loop-triangle tessellation
M-BVH.definition: core TriBVH candidate sets equal brute-force box overlap (self and cross); branch-and-bound distance equals brute force
M-BVH.failure_modes: Blender BVHTree candidates are bounding-volume pairs, not confirmed intersections
M-BVH.proves: no candidate is lost by the acceleration structure on the tested configurations

M-PROX-CLASS.geometry: base (unmodified) mesh data, Blender loop-triangle tessellation
M-PROX-CLASS.definition: no approved proximity requirement exists; any bucketing is experimental
M-PROX-CLASS.failure_modes: an invented threshold would be mistaken for a requirement
M-PROX-CLASS.tolerance: proximity_search_radius is a reporting scope (EXPERIMENTAL), not a defect threshold

M-XCHECK.property: Agreement of the core intersection classifier with independent implementations
M-XCHECK.definition: core proper-crossing pair set vs Blender BVHTree.overlap (own float32 triangle test, semantics pinned by B-INT-04); every disagreement adjudicated by exact rational arithmetic
M-XCHECK.includes: body mesh pairs with overlapping boxes
M-XCHECK.failure_modes: Blender's float32 test can miss crossings exact arithmetic confirms; its treatment of coplanar/touching triangles is not documented
M-XCHECK.proves: where core and Blender agree/disagree and which is right per exact arithmetic
M-XCHECK.cannot_prove: correctness of geometry the oracle was not run on (disagreements only)

M-SOL-VOLUME.property: Volume of the solid intersection A n B of two closed body shells
M-SOL-VOLUME.definition: Boolean INTERSECT volume (divergence theorem on the evaluated result) on in-memory copies whose components are oriented outward by their signed volume; exact for convex operands (pure backend). Validated when both kernels agree, both operand orders agree and V(A n B) + V(A minus B) = V(A).
M-SOL-VOLUME.includes: body mesh pairs with definite triangle intersections, both operands closed
M-SOL-VOLUME.transforms: full object matrix_world, baked into world coordinates
M-SOL-VOLUME.geometry: base (unmodified) mesh data; modifiers not applied
M-SOL-VOLUME.failure_modes: open, non-manifold, degenerate (not refinable) or winding-inconsistent operands are refused; kernel disagreement or identity failure leaves the value unvalidated; multi-component operands assume non-overlapping components; a refined copy is accepted only with REFINEMENT concordance (M-SOL-REFINE)
M-SOL-VOLUME.proves: the overlap volume of the stated solids, to the kernel and tolerance stated
M-SOL-VOLUME.cannot_prove: that the overlap is unintended, or that the solids represent the robot's real surfaces

M-SOL-DEPTH-AXIAL.property: Upper bound on the minimum translation distance (penetration depth) of two closed shells
M-SOL-DEPTH-AXIAL.definition: For each world axis direction d, t(d) is a verified separating translation of A along d: A moved by t(d)*d has overlap volume <= penetration_null_volume (primary kernel) and no proper triangle-surface crossing deeper than tri_contact (certificate); a uniform scan (penetration_axial_scan_samples) selects the first null sample and flags sampled reappearance of the overlap. axial_separation_bound = min over d of t(d). Every feasible separating translation has length >= MTD, so the bound is an UPPER BOUND on the minimum translation distance, to within about tri_contact. It equals MTD for axis-aligned boxes only.
M-SOL-DEPTH-AXIAL.failure_modes: NOT the minimum translation distance for general shapes (only six directions; e.g. sqrt(2) times MTD for a 45 degree face, U-SOL-13); the value along an axis need not be the first separation when overlap vanishes and reappears (non-convex or disconnected shapes) and the scan sees only gaps wider than T/penetration_axial_scan_samples (U-SOL-11, U-SOL-12); a null-volume test alone under-reports sharp-tip penetration by up to ~1e-4 m (U-SOL-14), which the surface-crossing certificate removes to ~tri_contact; directions that fail to verify or certify are listed and excluded
M-SOL-DEPTH-AXIAL.proves: a verified translation of this length along one axis removes the overlap volume and all proper surface crossings deeper than tri_contact, i.e. an upper bound on the minimum translation distance
M-SOL-DEPTH-AXIAL.cannot_prove: the exact penetration depth, the minimum translation distance, or the direction of least resistance for non-box shapes

M-SOL-REFINE.property: Measurement-copy refinement of a closed shell refused only for DEGENERATE_FACE, with a preservation proof
M-SOL-REFINE.definition: On an in-memory copy: (1) merge bit-identical vertices (exact), then (2) collapse clusters of vertices joined by edges <= zero_length_edge (1e-6 m) to their centroid and drop the faces that collapse. The copy is accepted only if the gate is clean, topology is closed manifold with the same components and orientation, every removed face is a sliver (altitude <= 1e-6 m), vertex displacement and sampled surface distance <= 1e-6 m, and the signed-volume change is within the swept-volume bound (surface area x distance). A pair measured on a copy is VOLUME_VALIDATED only if the unrefined shells give the same overlap volume through both kernels to volume_solver_agreement_rel.
M-SOL-REFINE.includes: operands whose ONLY gate reason is DEGENERATE_FACE
M-SOL-REFINE.geometry: base mesh data copied in memory; the .blend is never written
M-SOL-REFINE.failure_modes: needle faces with no short edge cannot be repaired (NOT_APPLICABLE); thin real solids below the edge tolerance are rejected by the acceptance tests (U-REF-07); sampled surface distance is a sample, not a proof, for removed faces
M-SOL-REFINE.proves: that the copy differs from the original by at most the stated displacement and removed slivers, and that the measured overlap volume is unchanged within the kernel agreement tolerance
M-SOL-REFINE.cannot_prove: that the original mesh is free of defects (it is not repaired); equivalence for any measurement other than the overlap volume and separation bound
